Out-of-band rates for a candidate and for held-out replicates

Source: R/metrics.R
outside_rates.Rd

"Inside the band in every cell" is a workable bar over six cells, where a genuine replicate clears it about a quarter of the time, but not over 72: a 1.28 SD band leaves a fifth of cells outside by construction, and no replicate clears it. This takes the bar from the IBM instead. Each replicate is held out and scored against the others, and the candidate is scored against the same reduced sets, so a claim can ask whether the candidate is outside less often than the best held-out replicate. That is stricter than treating the candidate as one more replicate: a deterministic model that tracks the centre should be outside far less often than a replicate, which scatters around it.

Usage

outside_rates(replicates, candidate, k = BAND_K)

Arguments

replicates

Matrix with replicates in rows and cells in columns; at least three rows.

candidate

Numeric vector of deterministic values, one per cell.

k

Half-width in standard deviations; see BAND_K.

Value

A list with candidate, the median over held-out sets of the fraction of cells in which the candidate is outside the band, and held_out, the fraction for each replicate scored against the others. Cells in which the replicates have no spread, or any value is not finite, are dropped.
